Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Multiple hyper-adrenergic symptoms (heat intolerance, palpitations, weight loss, libido loss) in a patient on thyroxine.  
• Episodic headaches, tingling, and shortness of breath temporally related to work stress.  
• No physical examination or laboratory data yet available.

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected iatrogenic hyperthyroidism secondary to excessive thyroxine replacement. Supported by medication history and classic hyper-thyroid symptom cluster (DDx likelihood: High).  

Considerations  
• Stress-related/anxiety or panic disorder with tension-type headaches (DDx likelihood: Medium).  
• Primary tension or migraine headaches precipitated by screen work (DDx likelihood: Medium).  
• Endogenous hyperthyroidism (Graves disease) – less likely but will be ruled out with thyroid function tests.  
• Intracranial mass lesion – low likelihood; consider if red-flag features develop.

Management/plan  
1. Schedule in-person consultation for complete physical examination (focus on thyroid gland, cardiovascular and neurological systems).  
2. Order laboratory studies: thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4, free T3), full blood count, electrolytes, renal & liver function, fasting glucose, lipids, vitamin B12 level.  
3. Consider ECG to evaluate palpitations.  
4. Review current thyroxine dose and adherence once results available; adjust or withhold medication if biochemically hyperthyroid.  
5. Provide education on stress management techniques; discuss workplace ergonomics for headache prevention.  
6. Safety net: advise to seek urgent care for severe persistent headache, focal neurological deficit, chest pain, or syncope.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism due to excessive thyroxine replacement – High likelihood; patient on thyroxine with classic hyper-thyroid symptom cluster (heat intolerance, palpitations, weight loss, libido loss).  
2. Stress-related/anxiety or panic disorder with tension-type headaches – Medium likelihood; symptoms occur mainly at stressful workplace, include palpitations, SOB, tingling, and headaches.  
3. Primary tension or migraine headaches – Medium likelihood; frontal severe headaches with mild nausea triggered by computer use.
